newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Earthquake rocks Taiwan, causing minor landslides.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks Taiwan, causing minor landslides.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale struck off Taiwan on Friday making buildings in the capital sway but no major damage was reported.
It was the biggest tremor to affect the island since 1973, meteorology officials said.
The earthquake, followed by nearly 150 minor aftershocks, struck at 7.43 a.m. (2243 GMT on Thursday) and caused minor landslides on an offshore island which blocked traffic, officials said.
The Central Weather Bureau said the epicentre was 40 km (25 miles) south of Taiwan's offshore southeastern island of Lanyu and the same distance beneath the earth's surface.
Earthquakes measuring 5.0-6.0 on the Richter scale are relatively common in Taiwan but rarely cause major damage.
The quake was felt in most parts of central and southern Taiwan and in Taipei where some buildings swayed for more than 20 seconds.
